column4: Here’s How Clorox Prioritizes Its Workforce’s Total Well-Being
column10: [NORTHAMPTON, MA / ACCESSWIRE / July 5, 2023 / The Clorox CompanyThe Clorox Company, Wednesday, July 5, 2023, Press release pictureClorox's ESG goals are integrated into our IGNITE strategy because we believe they drive growth and create positive value for our brands, people and communities. We've focused on where we can make the biggest impact - Clean World, Healthy Lives and Thriving Communities - and have 20 public-facing goals in these areas.In this installment of our "Steps to … " series, we spoke with Laura Baruch, our vice president of Total Rewards and sponsor of the Mental Health Champions ERG, about how Clorox is prioritizing total well-being, with a focus on our work around mental health, for our teammates and their families.Why is promoting health and well-being fundamental to Clorox?As a company with a diverse portfolio of wellness-related brands reaching households around the globe, we understand that we can only deliver on our purpose when our people are equipped to be well and thrive. To us, this means protecting the safety of our teammates and supporting their total well-being - at work and beyond.We often talk about our holistic approach to supporting the physical, mental and financial health of our people. We back that up by providing a powerful combination of benefits, programs and resources tailored to the diverse needs of our global workforce. Consistent with our IGNITE strategy, we put people at the center and genuinely embrace our responsibility to enhance the health and well-being of all our Clorox teammates and their families.From an ESG perspective, how do you evaluate and track something so personal as health and well-being?While our approach aims to empower our teammates to take ownership of their own wellness journeys, we as an employer have made bold commitments to ensure we're doing our part to foster an environment that enables them to do so. This includes:Promoting workplace safety: We closely monitor our operations and continually educate our teammates on how to identify, control or eliminate physical risk. This effort is just one of the ways Clorox has worked to maintain a recordable incident rate significantly below our target and the industry average.Ensuring financial well-being: We offer market-leading retirement benefits and no-cost financial coaching services to help our teammates prepare and save for retirement. These resources assist with budgeting, retirement planning, estimating healthcare expenses, insurance needs and more. Clorox is committed to supporting our teammates' financial well-being, which is why we've set an aspirational retirement readiness goal of 75% (as measured by a metric called the income replacement ratio).Encouraging preventive physical and mental health care: It can be challenging to measure our teammates' well-being, but we believe the key to driving better health outcomes is encouraging our people to get their preventive health screenings. Our goal is to have one-third of eligible teammates complete their age-based preventive health screenings every year. While I'm proud 29% took advantage of this benefit last year (exceeding our industry benchmark by 3 points), we have more progress to make!Story continuesWe understand these goals and metrics only reflect the wellness of our workforce in a few areas, so we're actively exploring how to measure the impact our benefits and resources have on the overall health of our people.Do Clorox's efforts to champion the overall well-being of its teammates include mental health?Mental health is unquestionably and intrinsically linked to our overall well-being. Not only does mental health directly impact our physical health, but it influences our ability to do our jobs well, feel fulfilled, connect with others, and contribute positively within our organization and the broader community. If we want to help people be well and thrive, mental health must be an integral part of how we support our team.While research tells us that one in four people will be affected by a mental illness at some point in their lives, it's important to remember we don't need a diagnosis in order to use resources to improve our own mental health. Every one of us experiences highs and lows in mental health. The recent rise in mental health concerns driven by the global pandemic has created a clear call to action for employers to not only destigmatize talking about mental health openly, including in the workplace, but also to offer mental health resources for teammates and their families.As we've navigated through the past few challenging years, I'm proud of how Clorox has supported our teammates, specifically with their mental well-being. Since 2020, we've enhanced our benefits by working with global partners to provide mental health resources, no-cost counseling sessions, education sessions, caregiver support and mindfulness tools to our global workforce.How do you prioritize which support structures and wellness resources to provide to a global workforce like we have at Clorox? Can you provide some examples specific to mental health?Championing well-being globally is an incredibly rewarding yet daunting endeavor, as there's no one-size-fits-all mobile app or program subscription that can tackle this challenge for everyone.That's why we've worked to establish a range of resources that support a number of different needs - from help finding a therapist, to tools for navigating day-to-day anxiety, to help with caregiving challenges. Here are just a few:As the executive sponsor of Clorox's Mental Health Champions employee resource group, I've witnessed first-hand how instrumental this community has been to raising awareness and destigmatizing mental health. This group helps Clorox identify gaps and opportunities to better support teammates' and their family members' mental health while providing a safe space for people to connect and share their experiences with resources that have helped them.We provide employee assistance programs globally, which offer supportive resources such as no-cost therapy sessions with counselors and trained clinicians to help with life transitions and family, legal, financial, and work issues. Additionally, we offer mindfulness resources as another form of preventive care to help manage stress, lessen anxiety and improve sleep year-round, not only in moments of crisis. Roughly 25% of our U.S. teammates have enrolled in this program within the past year, a level of engagement that is both unprecedented and indicative of how critical this support really is.One of our most highly regarded benefits are monthly Quiet Days, when we ask all teammates to not schedule meetings and to limit emails so they're able to focus on key priorities or take time off to recharge. We also recently reframed our sick leave - now called Health and Mental Well-Being Time Off- to be more inclusive of mental health needs for teammates and their families.What are some examples of mental health education, training and/or resources you would encourage other organizations to adopt?Our commitment to supporting mental health as part of overall well-being is one of the many reasons so many of my teammates and I are proud to work at Clorox. Here are a few tips to keep in mind when evaluating how best to support your workforce:Understand what your teammates need. Conduct internal surveys and/or focus groups to understand what resources your workforce values most and where there are opportunities to expand the support provided to your teammates and their families.Reduce the stigma by openly talking about mental health within your organization. Having senior leaders talk about the importance of mental health and potentially share how it has impacted their lives is truly impactful, and opens the door for others to share their own experiences.Create forums for teammates to learn and share insights about mental health. Schedule workshops; bring in external speakers who are subject matter experts; and offer mental health first-aid training to help your teammates identify, understand and respond to signs of mental health challenges. Most importantly, provide both in-person and virtual opportunities for teammates to connect with each other.Our ESG commitment is driven by our purpose to champion people to be well and thrive every single day. column4: Clorox (NYSE:CLX) shareholders have endured a 25% loss from investing in the stock three years ago
column10: [As an investor its worth striving to ensure your overall portfolio beats the market average. But its virtually certain that sometimes you will buy stocks that fall short of the market average returns. We regret to report that long term The Clorox Company (NYSE:CLX) shareholders have had that experience, with the share price dropping 31% in three years, versus a market return of about 37%.Since shareholders are down over the longer term, lets look at the underlying fundamentals over the that time and see if they've been consistent with returns. See our latest analysis for Clorox While markets are a powerful pricing mechanism, share prices reflect investor sentiment, not just underlying business performance. By comparing earnings per share (EPS) and share price changes over time, we can get a feel for how investor attitudes to a company have morphed over time.During the three years that the share price fell, Clorox's earnings per share (EPS) dropped by 56% each year. In comparison the 12% compound annual share price decline isn't as bad as the EPS drop-off. So the market may not be too worried about the EPS figure, at the moment -- or it may have previously priced some of the drop in. This positive sentiment is also reflected in the generous P/E ratio of 263.94.The image below shows how EPS has tracked over time (if you click on the image you can see greater detail).earnings-per-share-growthDive deeper into Clorox's key metrics by checking this interactive graph of Clorox's earnings, revenue and cash flow.What About Dividends?When looking at investment returns, it is important to consider the difference between total shareholder return (TSR) and share price return. The TSR incorporates the value of any spin-offs or discounted capital raisings, along with any dividends, based on the assumption that the dividends are reinvested. Arguably, the TSR gives a more comprehensive picture of the return generated by a stock. In the case of Clorox, it has a TSR of -25% for the last 3 years. That exceeds its share price return that we previously mentioned. This is largely a result of its dividend payments!Story continuesA Different PerspectiveIt's nice to see that Clorox shareholders have received a total shareholder return of 15% over the last year. And that does include the dividend. That gain is better than the annual TSR over five years, which is 6%. Therefore it seems like sentiment around the company has been positive lately. Given the share price momentum remains strong, it might be worth taking a closer look at the stock, lest you miss an opportunity. While it is well worth considering the different impacts that market conditions can have on the share price, there are other factors that are even more important. column4: Church & Dwight (CHD) Shares Up 21.9% YTD: What's Driving It?
column10: [Shares of Church & Dwight Co., Inc. CHD have rallied 21.9% so far this year. The company’s strength across its businesses, accretive acquisitions, effective pricing actions and shareholder-friendly policies seem to have boosted sentiments for the stock.The Ewing, NJ-based company belongs to the Zacks Soap and Cleaning Materials industry, which comes under the ambit of the Zacks Consumer Staples sector.Church & Dwight has a $24 billion market capitalization and currently carries a Zacks Rank #2 (Buy).Zacks Investment ResearchImage Source: Zacks Investment ResearchYear-to-date, the company’s shares have outperformed the industry’s decline of 0.2%. Notably, the S&P 500 has risen by 15.6%, while the sector dropped 2.8% during the same period.Catalysts Behind the Share Price IncreaseChurch & Dwight has been enjoying robust momentum in its household and personal care end markets, supported by solid demand for its products. The company reported strong first-quarter 2023 results, wherein both top and bottom lines increased year over year.CHD registered net sales of $1,429.8 million, reflecting an increase of 10.2% year over year and beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of $1,352 million. Its adjusted earnings came in at 85 cents per share, beating the Zacks Consensus Estimate of 76 cents. For instance, in the first quarter, the company’s online sales, as a percentage of total sales, came in at 16.3%. CL has a trailing four-quarter earnings surprise of 1.4%, on average.Clorox is a leading manufacturer of consumer and professional products worldwide. The TSR incorporates the value of any spin-offs or discounted capital raisings, along with any dividends, based on the assumption that the dividends are reinvested. Arguably, the TSR gives a more comprehensive picture of the return generated by a stock. In the case of Clorox, it has a TSR of -25% for the last 3 years. That exceeds its share price return that we previously mentioned. This is largely a result of its dividend payments!Story continuesA Different PerspectiveIt's nice to see that Clorox shareholders have received a total shareholder return of 15% over the last year. Given the share price momentum remains strong, it might be worth taking a closer look at the stock, lest you miss an opportunity. column4: Clorox (CLX) Gains From Digital Initiatives & Pricing Power
column10: [The Clorox Company’s CLX impressive performance can be attributed to a strong innovation pipeline, digital transformation initiatives, effective pricing strategies and cost-saving efforts. CLX plans to invest $500 million over the next five years in transformative technologies and processes. This includes replacing the enterprise resource planning (ERP) system, transitioning to a cloud-based platform and implementing other digital technologies.Clorox is taking a proactive approach to addressing persistent cost inflation. By implementing a combination of pricing and cost-saving efforts, the company aims to mitigate the impacts of rising costs and maintain its profitability.Thanks to its IGNITE strategy, emphasis on digital initiatives and focus on international business strength, the stock has outpaced the Zacks Soap and Cleaning Materials industry. This model aims to simplify the company's operations and increase efficiency in various areas such as supply chain, digital commerce, innovation and brand building. column4: 3 Undervalued Dividend Stocks to Consider Buying Now
column10: [When the going gets tough, investors start buying dividend stocks. And with good reason. Dividend stocks outperform non-income-generating stocks by a wide margin. They provide a solid foundation to build a retirement portfolio.Not only do investors get extra money put into their accounts, which helps to hedge against stock market downturns, but they’re a pretty good indicator the company paying them is financially sound. What makes that investing strategy even better is when you can find undervalued dividend stocks. You get the income, the downside protection, and the future potential of capital appreciation. It’s a triple play of opportunity—the following three dividend stocks off all three prongs for success.InvestorPlace - Stock Market News, Stock Advice & Trading TipsContinue reading for more information on how buying dividend stocks can help you reach your income goals.Clorox (CLX)A photo of a paper with a chart and the word "Dividends" written on it, with a pen and calculator resting on top of it.Source: jittawit21/Shutterstock.comAlthough best known for its namesake bleach, Clorox (NYSE:CLX) has a global portfolio of name-brand products. They include Pine-Sol and Formula 409 cleaners, Kingsford charcoal, and Brita water filters. Clorox brands often rank as the #1 or #2 market share product in their respective categories. Its main competitors are often grocery store private label brands. These core products account for over 80% of Clorox’s total revenue.These top-of-mind brands allow Clorox to charge a premium that helps bolster its bottom line. That’s important because the runaway inflation that hurt consumers also hit Clorox. It’s been working to take pricing and build back margins eroded by the economic setbacks.Part of that will be achieved by focusing on its core product lines and possibly selling non-core businesses. Vitamins, for example, have been a drag on performance. Clorox took a  $267 million write-down in 2021. It took another $445 million writedown last quarter and has been rumored to be looking to sell off the business.Story continuesClorox stock is down 13% from recent highs. Although shares are up 10% year to date, it trails the performance of the S&P 500, which has gained more than 17% in 2023. The bleach maker’s dividend currently yields 3.1% annually. It has paid a dividend yearly since 1970 and has increased the payout since 1978. That makes it a Dividend Aristocrat and should be considered by everyone investing for income.This company shows why it’s worthwhile buying dividend stocks in any economic situation.AT&T (T)Image of computer servers lined up in a dark roomSource: Gorodenkoff/Shutterstock.comThe old saying “when it rains, it pours” applies to telecom giant AT&T (NYSE:T). With analysts already concerned about its ability to generate free cash flow, a recent Wall Street Journal story about old, buried lead-lined cables created a new cloud of worries.In short, old, underground phone lines wrapped in lead could be leaching toxic lead into the surrounding soil and water. The Journal said its tests showed contamination under and beside the wires but dropped off further away. That suggests the cables are causing the problem. It further alleges AT&T management knew of the issue for decades. Also at risk are Verizon (NYSE:VZ) and other telecoms that were spun off from Ma Bell.AT&T disputes the allegations. In a statement, the telecom said, “The Journal’s reporting conflicts not only with what independent experts and long-standing science have stated about the safety of lead-clad telecom cables but also our testing, which we have made available to the public and shared with The Journal.”It’s an issue that will weigh on the stock for some time. It could be costly remediation, but it creates an opportunity for long-term investors. The stock is trading at just five times earnings estimates, at a fraction of its revenue, and less than 20 times the free cash flow it produces. Its dividend is yielding 7.8% annually as a result. These are rock-bottom valuations. The stock trades at levels not seen since the 1990s. It’s an undervalued dividend stock to consider buying now.Stanley Black & Decker (SWK)An image of US currency. dividend stocks for steady incomeSource: ShutterstockProfessional / Shutterstock.comEven though Stanley Black & Decker (NYSE:SWK) is up 28% this year, shares remain more than 55% below the all-time high they hit in 2021. There is plenty more room for this dividend-paying stock to achieve.Stanley is the premier tool-making company that has gathered under its umbrella some of the top brands on the market. Beyond its namesake brands, it owns Bostitch, Craftsman, DeWalt, Irwin, Mac Tools, and Porter-Cable.Stanley Black & Decker is amid a turnaround. Its restructuring plan is actually achieving its goals, which accounts for the rebound in its stock. Having pursued a growth-by-acquisition strategy over the years, the toolmaker is now cutting costs and reducing ballooning inventory. It aims to achieve $1 billion in cost cuts by the end of this year and some $2 billion over the next several years.The company was a beneficiary of the soaring housing market and the DIY boom of the pandemic, but the immediate future is undoubtedly cloudier. Home sales are softening, and rising interest rates don’t help. What will keep Stanley’s momentum moving forward will be able to keep hitting its turnaround targets.The stock trades at less than 20 times next year’s earnings estimates and a fraction of its sales. Its dividend yields 3.3% annually. Few companies have paid a dividend for as long as Stanley: 146 years, and increased the payout yearly since 1967, making it a Dividend King. Those companies have raised their dividends for 50 consecutive years or more.On the date of publication, Rich Duprey held a LONG positions in CLX and T stock. column4: 20 Most Trusted Professions in America
column10: [In this article, we will look at 20 Most Trusted Professions in America. We will also explore the dynamics and trends of trust building today along with some companies that are making some real efforts to build trust with the public. If you want to skip our detailed analysis, head straight to 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.The trust in professionals is often found be continually evolving, even though it does tend to stay constant for some specific professions. The evolution of trust underscore shifts in societal values, technological advancements, and new challenges that arise over time.Lack of Trust in Institutions TodayAccording to IMF, the lack of trust in institutions due to corruption is a pressing global issue. In 20 out of 28 surveyed countries, the average trust in institutions is below 50%. The IMF's research shows corruption hampers economic growth, investment, tax revenues, income distribution, and inclusive growth. To address this, the IMF is enhancing its engagement by deepening, lengthening, and broadening its analysis. It recognizes that criminal enforcement alone cannot cure corruption; instead, it focuses on transparency, robust institutions, and clear regulations.Digitalization often offers potential solutions, with electronic tax transactions that can somewhat reduce cross-border fraud. However, corruption as a global problem, requires a global response. The IMF emphasizes restoring trust in institutions is crucial to tackling pressing economic challenges such as inequality, climate change, and productivity growth.Trends Observed for Trust-Building in the Professional WorldOne prominent emerging trend is the increasing reliance on digital platforms and technology-driven services. In an era where online interactions are more prevalent than ever, professions related to cybersecurity, data Privacy, and online identity protection have taken center stage. Even though hacking is considered one of the least trusted jobs, ethical hacking is equally trusted and well compensated. Thus, professionals in these fields play a crucial role in safeguarding personal and corporate data from the ever-present threat of cyberattacks, and hence, trust in the authenticity of digitalization is built.Story continuesFor example, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has come up with its "My Ad Center" which is a portal for restoring digital trust by giving users control over ad preferences, personalized content, and insights into ad targeting criteria. Concerns about data access prompted this step and allowed users to block sensitive ads and opt-out of personalization tools. While it empowers users, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has been at the risk of potential financial risks if users turn off ads from certain industries. Nevertheless, the initiative shows Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG)’s commitment to building trust amid evolving privacy concerns and prepares for the changing ad-tracking landscape.Moreover, there is growing emphasis on sustainable practices and environmental stewardship. With increased awareness of climate change and its impact on the planet, professionals working in renewable energy, eco-friendly businesses, and sustainability consulting are gaining unprecedent recognition. These professions contribute largely to building trust in industries that prioritize ethical practices and eco-consciousness.We can look at how the Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s commitment to sustainability has led to its top ranking on Barron's 2023 100 Most Sustainable Companies list. For five consecutive years, Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX) has demonstrated its dedication to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) efforts which has earned trust from the public and customers. Their remarkable achievements include reducing greenhouse gas emissions, sourcing renewable energy, attaining zero-waste-to-landfill status, and maintaining pay equity across gender and race/ethnicity. These initiatives reflect Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s mission to promote well-being and flourishing communities and cultivate transparency and diversity in corporate governance.20 Most Trusted Professions In Americag-stockstudio/Shutterstock.comOur MethodologyTo list the most trusted professions in America, we have used multiple sources along with a number of reddit threads about the jobs which were most trusted. We made a list of 30 such professions, and only 20 of those most frequently appearing were included in our list.We gave each job an Insider Monkey (IM) score on the trust level based on consensus. Hence, the highest score indicates the highest trust, which means the profession is the most trusted.Please note that the list is highly subjective and does not comment on any individual’s integrity. The list is purely based on the perception of the common people’s trust in these professions.Here is a list of the 20 Most Trusted Professions in America  20. VeterinariansIM Score: 7.80Veterinarians are highly trusted and respected owing to their contribution to animal welfare and compassion towards animals. They are also considered people with harmless jobs with expertise in providing exclusive medical care for pets and animals. Thus, their humble profession and passion for treating animals earn them the admiration and trust of the wider community, particularly pet lovers. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.19. EngineersIM Score: 7.85Engineers are often highly regarded because of their educated and specialized knowledge in solving complex problems. They design, innovate, and create solutions for various industries, which is considered a huge support to the big organizations and hence, earns them respect. Moreover, their decent approach to projects and their knack for simplifying intricate concepts further their reputation as valuable contributors to society. Hence, we could say it is also considered one of the most ethical jobs.18. LibrariansIM Score: 7.90Americans trust librarians because they are considered knowledgeable, reliable, and non-judgmental sources of information. Librarians are trained professionals who assist in research, provide access to diverse resources, and promote literacy and learning. They uphold the values of intellectual freedom, privacy, and equitable access to information which gets them the respect and confidence of the community they serve.17. AccountantsIM Score: 7.95Accountants’ adherence to strict ethical standards, dedication to financial integrity, and commitment to helping individuals and businesses with financial decisions build trust in their expertise. They are seen as highly skilled and honest professionals crucial in managing financial matters, maintaining accuracy, and providing transparent financial information.16. PilotsIM Score: 8.1Pilots undergo extensive training and are experts with responsibility for passengers' safety. They have rigorous educational backgrounds and ongoing evaluations to ensure their skills remain top-notch. Their consistency in adhering to safety protocols and making critical decisions during flights instills confidence in passengers. It is one of the most presitigious jobs in the world.15. FirefightersIM Score: 8.3Firefighters face dangerous and challenging situations with extraordinary bravery, making split-second decisions to protect communities from fires and other emergencies. Their extensive training and readiness to put their lives on the line make their job one of the most respected in the world.14. ScientistsIM Score: 8.35Scientists are highly esteemed and trusted for expanding knowledge through research and discoveries. They are trusted for their adherence to scientific rigor and empiricism. Their contributions to sustainability efforts, global challenges, and rigorous education and expertise make them respected figures devoted to advancing society. It is one of the most trusted jobs in USA.13. PharmacistsIM Score: 8.4Pharmacists ensure safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, offer valuable drug-related information, and counsel patients. Their commitment to patient well-being, ethical practices, and accessibility makes them highly respected healthcare team members, promoting trust among the public.12. Paramedics/EMTs (Emergency Medical Technicians)IM Score: 8.5Paramedics are essential and trusted for their critical role in emergency medical care. They provide rapid response and life-saving interventions during accidents, medical crises, and disasters. Their advanced training, ability to remain calm under pressure, and dedication to saving lives earn them the trust and gratitude of the public. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.11. JudgesIM Score: 8.65Judges are trusted professionals owing to their impartiality and legal expertise. Americans are confident that judges will always ensure fair and just outcomes in legal proceedings.10. Religious Leaders (Clergy)IM Score: 8.70Religious leaders are vital in guiding spiritual growth while providing moral guidance. They offer huge support to their believers during challenging times. Their compassion, wisdom, and spirituality instill peace and builds trust among their followers.9. TeachersIM Score: 8.9Teachers are instrumental in shaping the minds and futures of students. They are experts passionate about creating a positive learning environment, and fostering trust and respect from students and parents alike. It is one of the jobs that still offer traditional pensions.8. Mental Health Counselors/PsychologistsIM Score: 9.1Mental health counselors offer invaluable support and therapy for individuals facing emotional and psychological challenges. Their expertise, empathy, and non-judgmental approach create a safe space, fostering trust and openness in therapeutic relationships.7. DentistsIM Score: 9.3Dentists have one of the highest paying jobs in the world. They are crucial for oral health and overall well-being of patients. Their skillset and professions allow them to provide ultimate comfort and dental support to their patients, building trust. This makes dental visits less daunting and ensure the best possible care for patients.6. Social WorkersIM Score: 9.35Social workers advocate for vulnerable populations and address societal issues. Their empathy and commitment to social justice gains the trust of individuals and communities as they provide much-needed support and resources.Click here to see 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.Suggested Articles:20 Least Trusted Professions in America20 Most Respected Professions in the World25 Most Profitable Professions in the WorldDisclosure: None.20 Most Trusted Professions in America is originally published on Insider Monkey]

column4: 3 Undervalued Dividend Stocks to Consider Buying Now
column10: [When the going gets tough, investors start buying dividend stocks. And with good reason. Dividend stocks outperform non-income-generating stocks by a wide margin. They provide a solid foundation to build a retirement portfolio.Not only do investors get extra money put into their accounts, which helps to hedge against stock market downturns, but they’re a pretty good indicator the company paying them is financially sound. What makes that investing strategy even better is when you can find undervalued dividend stocks. You get the income, the downside protection, and the future potential of capital appreciation. It’s a triple play of opportunity—the following three dividend stocks off all three prongs for success.InvestorPlace - Stock Market News, Stock Advice & Trading TipsContinue reading for more information on how buying dividend stocks can help you reach your income goals.Clorox (CLX)A photo of a paper with a chart and the word "Dividends" written on it, with a pen and calculator resting on top of it.Source: jittawit21/Shutterstock.comAlthough best known for its namesake bleach, Clorox (NYSE:CLX) has a global portfolio of name-brand products. They include Pine-Sol and Formula 409 cleaners, Kingsford charcoal, and Brita water filters. Clorox brands often rank as the #1 or #2 market share product in their respective categories. Its main competitors are often grocery store private label brands. These core products account for over 80% of Clorox’s total revenue.These top-of-mind brands allow Clorox to charge a premium that helps bolster its bottom line. That’s important because the runaway inflation that hurt consumers also hit Clorox. It’s been working to take pricing and build back margins eroded by the economic setbacks.Part of that will be achieved by focusing on its core product lines and possibly selling non-core businesses. Vitamins, for example, have been a drag on performance. Clorox took a  $267 million write-down in 2021. It took another $445 million writedown last quarter and has been rumored to be looking to sell off the business.Story continuesClorox stock is down 13% from recent highs. Although shares are up 10% year to date, it trails the performance of the S&P 500, which has gained more than 17% in 2023. The bleach maker’s dividend currently yields 3.1% annually. It has paid a dividend yearly since 1970 and has increased the payout since 1978. That makes it a Dividend Aristocrat and should be considered by everyone investing for income.This company shows why it’s worthwhile buying dividend stocks in any economic situation.AT&T (T)Image of computer servers lined up in a dark roomSource: Gorodenkoff/Shutterstock.comThe old saying “when it rains, it pours” applies to telecom giant AT&T (NYSE:T). With analysts already concerned about its ability to generate free cash flow, a recent Wall Street Journal story about old, buried lead-lined cables created a new cloud of worries.In short, old, underground phone lines wrapped in lead could be leaching toxic lead into the surrounding soil and water. The Journal said its tests showed contamination under and beside the wires but dropped off further away. That suggests the cables are causing the problem. It further alleges AT&T management knew of the issue for decades. Also at risk are Verizon (NYSE:VZ) and other telecoms that were spun off from Ma Bell.AT&T disputes the allegations. In a statement, the telecom said, “The Journal’s reporting conflicts not only with what independent experts and long-standing science have stated about the safety of lead-clad telecom cables but also our testing, which we have made available to the public and shared with The Journal.”It’s an issue that will weigh on the stock for some time. It could be costly remediation, but it creates an opportunity for long-term investors. The stock is trading at just five times earnings estimates, at a fraction of its revenue, and less than 20 times the free cash flow it produces. Its dividend is yielding 7.8% annually as a result. These are rock-bottom valuations. The stock trades at levels not seen since the 1990s. It’s an undervalued dividend stock to consider buying now.Stanley Black & Decker (SWK)An image of US currency. dividend stocks for steady incomeSource: ShutterstockProfessional / Shutterstock.comEven though Stanley Black & Decker (NYSE:SWK) is up 28% this year, shares remain more than 55% below the all-time high they hit in 2021. There is plenty more room for this dividend-paying stock to achieve.Stanley is the premier tool-making company that has gathered under its umbrella some of the top brands on the market. Beyond its namesake brands, it owns Bostitch, Craftsman, DeWalt, Irwin, Mac Tools, and Porter-Cable.Stanley Black & Decker is amid a turnaround. Its restructuring plan is actually achieving its goals, which accounts for the rebound in its stock. Having pursued a growth-by-acquisition strategy over the years, the toolmaker is now cutting costs and reducing ballooning inventory. It aims to achieve $1 billion in cost cuts by the end of this year and some $2 billion over the next several years.The company was a beneficiary of the soaring housing market and the DIY boom of the pandemic, but the immediate future is undoubtedly cloudier. Home sales are softening, and rising interest rates don’t help. What will keep Stanley’s momentum moving forward will be able to keep hitting its turnaround targets.The stock trades at less than 20 times next year’s earnings estimates and a fraction of its sales. Its dividend yields 3.3% annually. Few companies have paid a dividend for as long as Stanley: 146 years, and increased the payout yearly since 1967, making it a Dividend King. Those companies have raised their dividends for 50 consecutive years or more.On the date of publication, Rich Duprey held a LONG positions in CLX and T stock. column4: 20 Most Trusted Professions in America
column10: [In this article, we will look at 20 Most Trusted Professions in America. We will also explore the dynamics and trends of trust building today along with some companies that are making some real efforts to build trust with the public. If you want to skip our detailed analysis, head straight to 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.The trust in professionals is often found be continually evolving, even though it does tend to stay constant for some specific professions. The evolution of trust underscore shifts in societal values, technological advancements, and new challenges that arise over time.Lack of Trust in Institutions TodayAccording to IMF, the lack of trust in institutions due to corruption is a pressing global issue. In 20 out of 28 surveyed countries, the average trust in institutions is below 50%. The IMF's research shows corruption hampers economic growth, investment, tax revenues, income distribution, and inclusive growth. To address this, the IMF is enhancing its engagement by deepening, lengthening, and broadening its analysis. It recognizes that criminal enforcement alone cannot cure corruption; instead, it focuses on transparency, robust institutions, and clear regulations.Digitalization often offers potential solutions, with electronic tax transactions that can somewhat reduce cross-border fraud. However, corruption as a global problem, requires a global response. The IMF emphasizes restoring trust in institutions is crucial to tackling pressing economic challenges such as inequality, climate change, and productivity growth.Trends Observed for Trust-Building in the Professional WorldOne prominent emerging trend is the increasing reliance on digital platforms and technology-driven services. In an era where online interactions are more prevalent than ever, professions related to cybersecurity, data Privacy, and online identity protection have taken center stage. Even though hacking is considered one of the least trusted jobs, ethical hacking is equally trusted and well compensated. Thus, professionals in these fields play a crucial role in safeguarding personal and corporate data from the ever-present threat of cyberattacks, and hence, trust in the authenticity of digitalization is built.Story continuesFor example, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has come up with its "My Ad Center" which is a portal for restoring digital trust by giving users control over ad preferences, personalized content, and insights into ad targeting criteria. Concerns about data access prompted this step and allowed users to block sensitive ads and opt-out of personalization tools. While it empowers users, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has been at the risk of potential financial risks if users turn off ads from certain industries. Nevertheless, the initiative shows Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG)’s commitment to building trust amid evolving privacy concerns and prepares for the changing ad-tracking landscape.Moreover, there is growing emphasis on sustainable practices and environmental stewardship. With increased awareness of climate change and its impact on the planet, professionals working in renewable energy, eco-friendly businesses, and sustainability consulting are gaining unprecedent recognition. These professions contribute largely to building trust in industries that prioritize ethical practices and eco-consciousness.We can look at how the Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s commitment to sustainability has led to its top ranking on Barron's 2023 100 Most Sustainable Companies list. For five consecutive years, Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX) has demonstrated its dedication to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) efforts which has earned trust from the public and customers. Their remarkable achievements include reducing greenhouse gas emissions, sourcing renewable energy, attaining zero-waste-to-landfill status, and maintaining pay equity across gender and race/ethnicity. These initiatives reflect Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s mission to promote well-being and flourishing communities and cultivate transparency and diversity in corporate governance.20 Most Trusted Professions In Americag-stockstudio/Shutterstock.comOur MethodologyTo list the most trusted professions in America, we have used multiple sources along with a number of reddit threads about the jobs which were most trusted. We made a list of 30 such professions, and only 20 of those most frequently appearing were included in our list.We gave each job an Insider Monkey (IM) score on the trust level based on consensus. Hence, the highest score indicates the highest trust, which means the profession is the most trusted.Please note that the list is highly subjective and does not comment on any individual’s integrity. The list is purely based on the perception of the common people’s trust in these professions.Here is a list of the 20 Most Trusted Professions in America  20. VeterinariansIM Score: 7.80Veterinarians are highly trusted and respected owing to their contribution to animal welfare and compassion towards animals. They are also considered people with harmless jobs with expertise in providing exclusive medical care for pets and animals. Thus, their humble profession and passion for treating animals earn them the admiration and trust of the wider community, particularly pet lovers. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.19. EngineersIM Score: 7.85Engineers are often highly regarded because of their educated and specialized knowledge in solving complex problems. They design, innovate, and create solutions for various industries, which is considered a huge support to the big organizations and hence, earns them respect. Moreover, their decent approach to projects and their knack for simplifying intricate concepts further their reputation as valuable contributors to society. Hence, we could say it is also considered one of the most ethical jobs.18. LibrariansIM Score: 7.90Americans trust librarians because they are considered knowledgeable, reliable, and non-judgmental sources of information. Librarians are trained professionals who assist in research, provide access to diverse resources, and promote literacy and learning. They uphold the values of intellectual freedom, privacy, and equitable access to information which gets them the respect and confidence of the community they serve.17. AccountantsIM Score: 7.95Accountants’ adherence to strict ethical standards, dedication to financial integrity, and commitment to helping individuals and businesses with financial decisions build trust in their expertise. They are seen as highly skilled and honest professionals crucial in managing financial matters, maintaining accuracy, and providing transparent financial information.16. PilotsIM Score: 8.1Pilots undergo extensive training and are experts with responsibility for passengers' safety. They have rigorous educational backgrounds and ongoing evaluations to ensure their skills remain top-notch. Their consistency in adhering to safety protocols and making critical decisions during flights instills confidence in passengers. It is one of the most presitigious jobs in the world.15. FirefightersIM Score: 8.3Firefighters face dangerous and challenging situations with extraordinary bravery, making split-second decisions to protect communities from fires and other emergencies. Their extensive training and readiness to put their lives on the line make their job one of the most respected in the world.14. ScientistsIM Score: 8.35Scientists are highly esteemed and trusted for expanding knowledge through research and discoveries. They are trusted for their adherence to scientific rigor and empiricism. Their contributions to sustainability efforts, global challenges, and rigorous education and expertise make them respected figures devoted to advancing society. It is one of the most trusted jobs in USA.13. PharmacistsIM Score: 8.4Pharmacists ensure safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, offer valuable drug-related information, and counsel patients. Their commitment to patient well-being, ethical practices, and accessibility makes them highly respected healthcare team members, promoting trust among the public.12. Paramedics/EMTs (Emergency Medical Technicians)IM Score: 8.5Paramedics are essential and trusted for their critical role in emergency medical care. They provide rapid response and life-saving interventions during accidents, medical crises, and disasters. Their advanced training, ability to remain calm under pressure, and dedication to saving lives earn them the trust and gratitude of the public. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.11. JudgesIM Score: 8.65Judges are trusted professionals owing to their impartiality and legal expertise. Americans are confident that judges will always ensure fair and just outcomes in legal proceedings.10. Religious Leaders (Clergy)IM Score: 8.70Religious leaders are vital in guiding spiritual growth while providing moral guidance. They offer huge support to their believers during challenging times. Their compassion, wisdom, and spirituality instill peace and builds trust among their followers.9. TeachersIM Score: 8.9Teachers are instrumental in shaping the minds and futures of students. They are experts passionate about creating a positive learning environment, and fostering trust and respect from students and parents alike. It is one of the jobs that still offer traditional pensions.8. Mental Health Counselors/PsychologistsIM Score: 9.1Mental health counselors offer invaluable support and therapy for individuals facing emotional and psychological challenges. Their expertise, empathy, and non-judgmental approach create a safe space, fostering trust and openness in therapeutic relationships.7. DentistsIM Score: 9.3Dentists have one of the highest paying jobs in the world. They are crucial for oral health and overall well-being of patients. Their skillset and professions allow them to provide ultimate comfort and dental support to their patients, building trust. This makes dental visits less daunting and ensure the best possible care for patients.6. Social WorkersIM Score: 9.35Social workers advocate for vulnerable populations and address societal issues. Their empathy and commitment to social justice gains the trust of individuals and communities as they provide much-needed support and resources.Click here to see 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.Suggested Articles:20 Least Trusted Professions in America20 Most Respected Professions in the World25 Most Profitable Professions in the WorldDisclosure: None.20 Most Trusted Professions in America is originally published on Insider Monkey]

column4: 20 Most Trusted Professions in America
column10: [In this article, we will look at 20 Most Trusted Professions in America. We will also explore the dynamics and trends of trust building today along with some companies that are making some real efforts to build trust with the public. If you want to skip our detailed analysis, head straight to 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.The trust in professionals is often found be continually evolving, even though it does tend to stay constant for some specific professions. The evolution of trust underscore shifts in societal values, technological advancements, and new challenges that arise over time.Lack of Trust in Institutions TodayAccording to IMF, the lack of trust in institutions due to corruption is a pressing global issue. In 20 out of 28 surveyed countries, the average trust in institutions is below 50%. The IMF's research shows corruption hampers economic growth, investment, tax revenues, income distribution, and inclusive growth. To address this, the IMF is enhancing its engagement by deepening, lengthening, and broadening its analysis. It recognizes that criminal enforcement alone cannot cure corruption; instead, it focuses on transparency, robust institutions, and clear regulations.Digitalization often offers potential solutions, with electronic tax transactions that can somewhat reduce cross-border fraud. However, corruption as a global problem, requires a global response. The IMF emphasizes restoring trust in institutions is crucial to tackling pressing economic challenges such as inequality, climate change, and productivity growth.Trends Observed for Trust-Building in the Professional WorldOne prominent emerging trend is the increasing reliance on digital platforms and technology-driven services. In an era where online interactions are more prevalent than ever, professions related to cybersecurity, data Privacy, and online identity protection have taken center stage. Even though hacking is considered one of the least trusted jobs, ethical hacking is equally trusted and well compensated. Thus, professionals in these fields play a crucial role in safeguarding personal and corporate data from the ever-present threat of cyberattacks, and hence, trust in the authenticity of digitalization is built.Story continuesFor example, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has come up with its "My Ad Center" which is a portal for restoring digital trust by giving users control over ad preferences, personalized content, and insights into ad targeting criteria. Concerns about data access prompted this step and allowed users to block sensitive ads and opt-out of personalization tools. While it empowers users, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has been at the risk of potential financial risks if users turn off ads from certain industries. Nevertheless, the initiative shows Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG)’s commitment to building trust amid evolving privacy concerns and prepares for the changing ad-tracking landscape.Moreover, there is growing emphasis on sustainable practices and environmental stewardship. With increased awareness of climate change and its impact on the planet, professionals working in renewable energy, eco-friendly businesses, and sustainability consulting are gaining unprecedent recognition. These professions contribute largely to building trust in industries that prioritize ethical practices and eco-consciousness.We can look at how the Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s commitment to sustainability has led to its top ranking on Barron's 2023 100 Most Sustainable Companies list. For five consecutive years, Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX) has demonstrated its dedication to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) efforts which has earned trust from the public and customers. Their remarkable achievements include reducing greenhouse gas emissions, sourcing renewable energy, attaining zero-waste-to-landfill status, and maintaining pay equity across gender and race/ethnicity. These initiatives reflect Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s mission to promote well-being and flourishing communities and cultivate transparency and diversity in corporate governance.20 Most Trusted Professions In Americag-stockstudio/Shutterstock.comOur MethodologyTo list the most trusted professions in America, we have used multiple sources along with a number of reddit threads about the jobs which were most trusted. We made a list of 30 such professions, and only 20 of those most frequently appearing were included in our list.We gave each job an Insider Monkey (IM) score on the trust level based on consensus. Hence, the highest score indicates the highest trust, which means the profession is the most trusted.Please note that the list is highly subjective and does not comment on any individual’s integrity. The list is purely based on the perception of the common people’s trust in these professions.Here is a list of the 20 Most Trusted Professions in America  20. VeterinariansIM Score: 7.80Veterinarians are highly trusted and respected owing to their contribution to animal welfare and compassion towards animals. They are also considered people with harmless jobs with expertise in providing exclusive medical care for pets and animals. Thus, their humble profession and passion for treating animals earn them the admiration and trust of the wider community, particularly pet lovers. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.19. EngineersIM Score: 7.85Engineers are often highly regarded because of their educated and specialized knowledge in solving complex problems. They design, innovate, and create solutions for various industries, which is considered a huge support to the big organizations and hence, earns them respect. Moreover, their decent approach to projects and their knack for simplifying intricate concepts further their reputation as valuable contributors to society. Hence, we could say it is also considered one of the most ethical jobs.18. LibrariansIM Score: 7.90Americans trust librarians because they are considered knowledgeable, reliable, and non-judgmental sources of information. Librarians are trained professionals who assist in research, provide access to diverse resources, and promote literacy and learning. They uphold the values of intellectual freedom, privacy, and equitable access to information which gets them the respect and confidence of the community they serve.17. AccountantsIM Score: 7.95Accountants’ adherence to strict ethical standards, dedication to financial integrity, and commitment to helping individuals and businesses with financial decisions build trust in their expertise. They are seen as highly skilled and honest professionals crucial in managing financial matters, maintaining accuracy, and providing transparent financial information.16. PilotsIM Score: 8.1Pilots undergo extensive training and are experts with responsibility for passengers' safety. They have rigorous educational backgrounds and ongoing evaluations to ensure their skills remain top-notch. Their consistency in adhering to safety protocols and making critical decisions during flights instills confidence in passengers. It is one of the most presitigious jobs in the world.15. FirefightersIM Score: 8.3Firefighters face dangerous and challenging situations with extraordinary bravery, making split-second decisions to protect communities from fires and other emergencies. Their extensive training and readiness to put their lives on the line make their job one of the most respected in the world.14. ScientistsIM Score: 8.35Scientists are highly esteemed and trusted for expanding knowledge through research and discoveries. They are trusted for their adherence to scientific rigor and empiricism. Their contributions to sustainability efforts, global challenges, and rigorous education and expertise make them respected figures devoted to advancing society. It is one of the most trusted jobs in USA.13. PharmacistsIM Score: 8.4Pharmacists ensure safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, offer valuable drug-related information, and counsel patients. Their commitment to patient well-being, ethical practices, and accessibility makes them highly respected healthcare team members, promoting trust among the public.12. Paramedics/EMTs (Emergency Medical Technicians)IM Score: 8.5Paramedics are essential and trusted for their critical role in emergency medical care. They provide rapid response and life-saving interventions during accidents, medical crises, and disasters. Their advanced training, ability to remain calm under pressure, and dedication to saving lives earn them the trust and gratitude of the public. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.11. JudgesIM Score: 8.65Judges are trusted professionals owing to their impartiality and legal expertise. Americans are confident that judges will always ensure fair and just outcomes in legal proceedings.10. Religious Leaders (Clergy)IM Score: 8.70Religious leaders are vital in guiding spiritual growth while providing moral guidance. They offer huge support to their believers during challenging times. Their compassion, wisdom, and spirituality instill peace and builds trust among their followers.9. TeachersIM Score: 8.9Teachers are instrumental in shaping the minds and futures of students. They are experts passionate about creating a positive learning environment, and fostering trust and respect from students and parents alike. It is one of the jobs that still offer traditional pensions.8. Mental Health Counselors/PsychologistsIM Score: 9.1Mental health counselors offer invaluable support and therapy for individuals facing emotional and psychological challenges. Their expertise, empathy, and non-judgmental approach create a safe space, fostering trust and openness in therapeutic relationships.7. DentistsIM Score: 9.3Dentists have one of the highest paying jobs in the world. They are crucial for oral health and overall well-being of patients. Their skillset and professions allow them to provide ultimate comfort and dental support to their patients, building trust. This makes dental visits less daunting and ensure the best possible care for patients.6. Social WorkersIM Score: 9.35Social workers advocate for vulnerable populations and address societal issues. Their empathy and commitment to social justice gains the trust of individuals and communities as they provide much-needed support and resources.Click here to see 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.Suggested Articles:20 Least Trusted Professions in America20 Most Respected Professions in the World25 Most Profitable Professions in the WorldDisclosure: None.20 Most Trusted Professions in America is originally published on Insider Monkey]

column4: 20 Most Trusted Professions in America
column10: [In this article, we will look at 20 Most Trusted Professions in America. We will also explore the dynamics and trends of trust building today along with some companies that are making some real efforts to build trust with the public. If you want to skip our detailed analysis, head straight to 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.The trust in professionals is often found be continually evolving, even though it does tend to stay constant for some specific professions. The evolution of trust underscore shifts in societal values, technological advancements, and new challenges that arise over time.Lack of Trust in Institutions TodayAccording to IMF, the lack of trust in institutions due to corruption is a pressing global issue. In 20 out of 28 surveyed countries, the average trust in institutions is below 50%. The IMF's research shows corruption hampers economic growth, investment, tax revenues, income distribution, and inclusive growth. To address this, the IMF is enhancing its engagement by deepening, lengthening, and broadening its analysis. It recognizes that criminal enforcement alone cannot cure corruption; instead, it focuses on transparency, robust institutions, and clear regulations.Digitalization often offers potential solutions, with electronic tax transactions that can somewhat reduce cross-border fraud. However, corruption as a global problem, requires a global response. The IMF emphasizes restoring trust in institutions is crucial to tackling pressing economic challenges such as inequality, climate change, and productivity growth.Trends Observed for Trust-Building in the Professional WorldOne prominent emerging trend is the increasing reliance on digital platforms and technology-driven services. In an era where online interactions are more prevalent than ever, professions related to cybersecurity, data Privacy, and online identity protection have taken center stage. Even though hacking is considered one of the least trusted jobs, ethical hacking is equally trusted and well compensated. Thus, professionals in these fields play a crucial role in safeguarding personal and corporate data from the ever-present threat of cyberattacks, and hence, trust in the authenticity of digitalization is built.Story continuesFor example, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has come up with its "My Ad Center" which is a portal for restoring digital trust by giving users control over ad preferences, personalized content, and insights into ad targeting criteria. Concerns about data access prompted this step and allowed users to block sensitive ads and opt-out of personalization tools. While it empowers users, Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG) has been at the risk of potential financial risks if users turn off ads from certain industries. Nevertheless, the initiative shows Alphabet Inc (NASDAQ:GOOG)’s commitment to building trust amid evolving privacy concerns and prepares for the changing ad-tracking landscape.Moreover, there is growing emphasis on sustainable practices and environmental stewardship. With increased awareness of climate change and its impact on the planet, professionals working in renewable energy, eco-friendly businesses, and sustainability consulting are gaining unprecedent recognition. These professions contribute largely to building trust in industries that prioritize ethical practices and eco-consciousness.We can look at how the Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s commitment to sustainability has led to its top ranking on Barron's 2023 100 Most Sustainable Companies list. For five consecutive years, Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX) has demonstrated its dedication to environmental, social, and governance (ESG) efforts which has earned trust from the public and customers. Their remarkable achievements include reducing greenhouse gas emissions, sourcing renewable energy, attaining zero-waste-to-landfill status, and maintaining pay equity across gender and race/ethnicity. These initiatives reflect Clorox Co (NYSE:CLX)’s mission to promote well-being and flourishing communities and cultivate transparency and diversity in corporate governance.20 Most Trusted Professions In Americag-stockstudio/Shutterstock.comOur MethodologyTo list the most trusted professions in America, we have used multiple sources along with a number of reddit threads about the jobs which were most trusted. We made a list of 30 such professions, and only 20 of those most frequently appearing were included in our list.We gave each job an Insider Monkey (IM) score on the trust level based on consensus. Hence, the highest score indicates the highest trust, which means the profession is the most trusted.Please note that the list is highly subjective and does not comment on any individual’s integrity. The list is purely based on the perception of the common people’s trust in these professions.Here is a list of the 20 Most Trusted Professions in America  20. VeterinariansIM Score: 7.80Veterinarians are highly trusted and respected owing to their contribution to animal welfare and compassion towards animals. They are also considered people with harmless jobs with expertise in providing exclusive medical care for pets and animals. Thus, their humble profession and passion for treating animals earn them the admiration and trust of the wider community, particularly pet lovers. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.19. EngineersIM Score: 7.85Engineers are often highly regarded because of their educated and specialized knowledge in solving complex problems. They design, innovate, and create solutions for various industries, which is considered a huge support to the big organizations and hence, earns them respect. Moreover, their decent approach to projects and their knack for simplifying intricate concepts further their reputation as valuable contributors to society. Hence, we could say it is also considered one of the most ethical jobs.18. LibrariansIM Score: 7.90Americans trust librarians because they are considered knowledgeable, reliable, and non-judgmental sources of information. Librarians are trained professionals who assist in research, provide access to diverse resources, and promote literacy and learning. They uphold the values of intellectual freedom, privacy, and equitable access to information which gets them the respect and confidence of the community they serve.17. AccountantsIM Score: 7.95Accountants’ adherence to strict ethical standards, dedication to financial integrity, and commitment to helping individuals and businesses with financial decisions build trust in their expertise. They are seen as highly skilled and honest professionals crucial in managing financial matters, maintaining accuracy, and providing transparent financial information.16. PilotsIM Score: 8.1Pilots undergo extensive training and are experts with responsibility for passengers' safety. They have rigorous educational backgrounds and ongoing evaluations to ensure their skills remain top-notch. Their consistency in adhering to safety protocols and making critical decisions during flights instills confidence in passengers. It is one of the most presitigious jobs in the world.15. FirefightersIM Score: 8.3Firefighters face dangerous and challenging situations with extraordinary bravery, making split-second decisions to protect communities from fires and other emergencies. Their extensive training and readiness to put their lives on the line make their job one of the most respected in the world.14. ScientistsIM Score: 8.35Scientists are highly esteemed and trusted for expanding knowledge through research and discoveries. They are trusted for their adherence to scientific rigor and empiricism. Their contributions to sustainability efforts, global challenges, and rigorous education and expertise make them respected figures devoted to advancing society. It is one of the most trusted jobs in USA.13. PharmacistsIM Score: 8.4Pharmacists ensure safe and accurate dispensing of prescriptions, offer valuable drug-related information, and counsel patients. Their commitment to patient well-being, ethical practices, and accessibility makes them highly respected healthcare team members, promoting trust among the public.12. Paramedics/EMTs (Emergency Medical Technicians)IM Score: 8.5Paramedics are essential and trusted for their critical role in emergency medical care. They provide rapid response and life-saving interventions during accidents, medical crises, and disasters. Their advanced training, ability to remain calm under pressure, and dedication to saving lives earn them the trust and gratitude of the public. It is one of the most trusted professions in America.11. JudgesIM Score: 8.65Judges are trusted professionals owing to their impartiality and legal expertise. Americans are confident that judges will always ensure fair and just outcomes in legal proceedings.10. Religious Leaders (Clergy)IM Score: 8.70Religious leaders are vital in guiding spiritual growth while providing moral guidance. They offer huge support to their believers during challenging times. Their compassion, wisdom, and spirituality instill peace and builds trust among their followers.9. TeachersIM Score: 8.9Teachers are instrumental in shaping the minds and futures of students. They are experts passionate about creating a positive learning environment, and fostering trust and respect from students and parents alike. It is one of the jobs that still offer traditional pensions.8. Mental Health Counselors/PsychologistsIM Score: 9.1Mental health counselors offer invaluable support and therapy for individuals facing emotional and psychological challenges. Their expertise, empathy, and non-judgmental approach create a safe space, fostering trust and openness in therapeutic relationships.7. DentistsIM Score: 9.3Dentists have one of the highest paying jobs in the world. They are crucial for oral health and overall well-being of patients. Their skillset and professions allow them to provide ultimate comfort and dental support to their patients, building trust. This makes dental visits less daunting and ensure the best possible care for patients.6. Social WorkersIM Score: 9.35Social workers advocate for vulnerable populations and address societal issues. Their empathy and commitment to social justice gains the trust of individuals and communities as they provide much-needed support and resources.Click here to see 5 Most Trusted Professions in America.Suggested Articles:20 Least Trusted Professions in America20 Most Respected Professions in the World25 Most Profitable Professions in the WorldDisclosure: None.20 Most Trusted Professions in America is originally published on Insider Monkey]

column4: Procter & Gamble CEO on 'very strong' earnings, price hikes, falling commodity prices
column10: [Procter and Gamble reported fiscal fourth quarter results that were slightly better than Wall Street had been anticipating, after getting a boost from higher prices. In an interview with Yahoo Finance Live, Procter and Gamble CEO Jon Moeller says the "consumer remains strong" and that they are looking for brands they know and trust. P&G does stand to benefit from a decline in commodity prices, with Moeller pointing specifically to the decline in petro and pulp prices, but he says labor costs and foreign exchange remain headwinds.Video Transcript- An improved inflation outlook and higher prices on products such as Tide led Procter & Gamble to a better than expected fiscal fourth quarter, though the consumer goods business gave a fiscal 2024 outlook short of Wall Street's expectations. Sales and profit grew in all of the company's segments in the quarter and the shares right now are trading higher. Yahoo Finance's Executive Editor Brian Sozzi spoke with P&G CEO John Muller on how he sees these results.JON MOELLER: Very strong. 8% organic sales growth, every category growing, five of the categories, so half of our portfolio growing double digits. 7 out of 10 categories building share. If you look at it on a geographic basis, same general story, every region growing. The US, our largest market, we grew 6% value share up 20 basis points, volume share up 50 basis points.And importantly, volume, which is going to be an increasingly important component of top line, is coming around. Take the US, for example, last quarters minus 3, minus 3, 0, plus 3 in the quarter we just completed. Strong earnings growth. 13% core earnings per share growth, 22% excluding currency. That all sets us up very well from a momentum standpoint as we head into our next fiscal year, which started 29 days ago.BRIAN SOZZI: Talk to us about the volume declines in some of the businesses. Are you seeing a softening US shopper?JON MOELLER: No. If you look on a global aggregate basis in the quarter we just completed, volume was minus 1. So very, very modest decline, which you would expect with the level of pricing that we've been taking. And as I mentioned, in the US, our largest market, volume plus 3. So consumer remains strong. They continue to value brands that are known and trusted that perform in categories where we focus our portfolio, where performance drives brand choice.Story continuesSo it's been a good, gratifying experience overall in terms of the strategy that we've been executing to build superiority of our brands, product package, communication, go-to market, and value, and that's being reflected in consumer behavior.BRIAN SOZZI: P&G has been in the enviable position, John, of having relatively smaller exposure to private label brands. I believe the stat from Evercore pegged it at about 18% of your portfolio leveraged to, or just competes, with private label. But within that 18%, in that number, I mean, do you see consumers trading down to private label?JON MOELLER: There are some consumers who are, but again, we're building share so that dynamic isn't pronounced by any stretch of the imagination. And we've given them an easier trade down path, if they choose it, within our portfolio, as we've extended the brands take tide, for example, now with the offering of Tide Simply, which we didn't have in the last economic turndown. So if they need to trade down, they can do it within our brands and maintain a very high performance level. There's some trade down to private label, but I think if you look over the last three years, we're talking small basis point increases in share while we've been simultaneously building share.BRIAN SOZZI: One number that jumps off this page-- and we haven't had we haven't been able to talk about this in some time, maybe two years lower, commodities cost, John. Wow. Within your next guidance, you've built-in $400 million in savings. I almost didn't think the day would ever come. Where are you seeing the biggest declines commodity wise?JON MOELLER: In the petro complex and in pulp are the primary areas. It's not all one way. There are commodities that continue to increase. Obviously, we're dealing with other cost pools as well, where the markets are tight like labor. And there's a significant foreign exchange headwinds still, about the same number, about $400 million after tax as we head into next year. So it's not all about roses, but it's a lot better looking than it was last year at this time, and our guidance reflects that.BRIAN SOZZI: Are you seeing-- I think it was this week. Coca-Cola CEO James Quincey coined it intense inflation overseas. Are you seeing that overseas in your markets, and then the US inflation picture starting to moderate?JON MOELLER: Well, definitely, the US picture is moderating some. There's still significant inflation in Europe, which may have been what James was referring to. And obviously, with a very unfortunate situation in the Eastern part of that continent, there's continued pressure on pricing just from a supply standpoint.BRIAN SOZZI: In terms of pricing, P&G and a lot of other consumer products, Giants, have been able to push through higher prices the past two years to offset some of that inflation. But well, now that it's slowing down, what do you do with prices? Are you able to take them down? Do you want to take them down? I mean, how do you think about it?JON MOELLER: Pricing has been a positive component of our top line growth for 49 out of the last 51 quarters. So it's part of our business model, which is driven by innovation, and to the extent that we can bring better, referred, more delightful products and experiences to consumers. There's a modest amount of pricing that that affords.BRIAN SOZZI: How would you grade the Chinese economy right now? Of course, you have exposure there through various segments. That economy, from the outside looking in, looks to have really slowed down. What are you seeing?JON MOELLER: Well, versus six months ago, it's really picked up. Versus 4, 5 years ago, it's a little bit slower. But we grew our business in China 4%. I expect that number to continue to increase modestly as we move on. But things are picking up.BRIAN SOZZI: Over the next 12 months, John, before I let you go, what products should investors most be excited about? We've talked repeatedly about increasing innovation at P&G. Do you have more breakthrough stuff coming?JON MOELLER: We always do. I'm not going to talk about future innovation, but you and I were talking before. We went on the air about our Dawn business, our hand dishwashing business, where we've had two major innovations, Dawn Powerwash and the Easy Squeeze bottle, the upside-down bottle. And behind those innovations across the US and Europe, we grew that business 17% last year. We built share 1 and 1/2 points in the US, 1.1 points, I think, the number was in Europe. So the team is constantly looking for ways to bring further delight to consumers, and I think those are two examples of doing that very well.BRIAN SOZZI: That brings up another good point. How does your team find some of these use cases? Because they ultimately help you to drive a higher price, higher sales, and better earnings. I didn't know I needed soap sprayed out of a bottle. I didn't know I needed a capless bottle, but to me it makes a lot of sense. What is the origin story of these things?JON MOELLER: The majority of it is just a proximity to and a deep understanding of consumers and their attention points. And once we understand those tension points, we try to solve them. So take the capitalist bottle. I don't know about you, but for years when I've watched this, it's kind of a messy experience, and the cap gets covered with the product over time, and no one likes that. So that's attention point, and our team was able to identify a solution.It wasn't easy, but generally overcame that issue and made it even easier to wash by just simply taking the bottle and dispensing as opposed to having to turn it upside-down. So these are little things that make a difference. And when you can solve them and do it in a delightful way, good things happen.- And that was John Mueller who was the CEO.]

This insight is at the core of our proprietary surprise prediction model -- the Zacks Earnings ESP (Expected Surprise Prediction).The Zacks Earnings ESP compares the Most Accurate Estimate to the Zacks Consensus Estimate for the quarter; the Most Accurate Estimate is a more recent version of the Zacks Consensus EPS estimate. The idea here is that analysts revising their estimates right before an earnings release have the latest information, which could potentially be more accurate than what they and others contributing to the consensus had predicted earlier.Story continuesThus, a positive or negative Earnings ESP reading theoretically indicates the likely deviation of the actual earnings from the consensus estimate.
